texts.orig: Q: We all know how crazy and busy it is to be a PM. What tips do you have for managing your time and workload?

texts.orig: Using your work time most productively is a never-ending struggle. PMs are particularly prone because they rarely have clear deadlines or well thought out Gantt charts, but this hits all professionals.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Though I thoroughly continue to struggle with time management myself, I have found a few tactics to be extremely effective. Here are my top five favorite strategies for making the most of my time:

texts.text: 2. Make it easy to know what to work on next

texts.label: text
texts.orig: When you do have time to work, how easily can you decide what to work on next?
texts.text: When you do have time to work, how easily can you decide what to work on next?

texts.text: a simple notebook

texts.label: text
texts.orig: (not an app). Every day, I write out my TODOs for the day, cross things off when they're done, and savor the sweet satisfaction of crumpling up the page when I knock out all of my tasks. Anything I don't get done that day, I re-write for the next day, which has the benefit of (1) reminding me of what I still need to get done, and (2) forcing me to re-evaluate whether I even need to do it.

texts.orig: 4. Prioritize and communicate
texts.text: 4. Prioritize and communicate

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Shifting priorities and last-minute asks are consistently one of my biggest time sucks. Here’s an exercise: When you’ve already got a full plate and your manager comes to you with more work, what do you usually say?
texts.text: Shifting priorities and last-minute asks are consistently one of my biggest time sucks. Here’s an exercise: When you’ve already got a full plate and your manager comes to you with more work, what do you usually say?

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The two wrong answers are:
texts.text: The two wrong answers are:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: Yes!
texts.text: Yes!

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: No!
texts.text: No!

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Wait, what? Well, assuming you agree it's a good idea (otherwise share your perspective openly and honestly), I've found a concept called "Prioritize and Communicate" invaluable. This is a technique my last manager taught me for when you are asked to take on more work. It is made up of two steps:
texts.text: Wait, what? Well, assuming you agree it's a good idea (otherwise share your perspective openly and honestly), I've found a concept called "Prioritize and Communicate" invaluable. This is a technique my last manager taught me for when you are asked to take on more work. It is made up of two steps:

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Prioritize
texts.text: Prioritize

texts.label: text
texts.orig: : Take this new ask and prioritize it amongst the work you already have.
texts.text: : Take this new ask and prioritize it amongst the work you already have.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Communicate
texts.text: Communicate

texts.label: text
texts.orig: : Tell your manager where you prioritized this ask.
texts.text: : Tell your manager where you prioritized this ask.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: For example, "Great idea Ms. Manager! I've added this to my priority list, right after X, Y, Z. Let me know if you disagree with that prioritization."
texts.text: For example, "Great idea Ms. Manager! I've added this to my priority list, right after X, Y, Z. Let me know if you disagree with that prioritization."

texts.label: text
texts.orig: If your manager is onboard with your prioritization, you're done. If not, take their feedback and go through this cycle again. Either way, you've avoided adding more immediate work, you're now on the same page about priorities, you've set clear expectations.
texts.text: If your manager is onboard with your prioritization, you're done. If not, take their feedback and go through this cycle again. Either way, you've avoided adding more immediate work, you're now on the same page about priorities, you've set clear expectations.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Also, it's easy to forget you can actually say no to asks. Whether it's your manager, your peer, or another PM, you can say no. YOU CAN SAY NO.

texts.orig: 5. Be prepared
texts.text: 5. Be prepared

texts.label: text
texts.orig: And finally, at the very core of effective time management is simply being prepared. The more ahead of everyone else you are, the easier everything gets.
texts.text: And finally, at the very core of effective time management is simply being prepared. The more ahead of everyone else you are, the easier everything gets.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Some tips for stay ahead:
texts.text: Some tips for stay ahead:

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Review your calendar
texts.text: Review your calendar

texts.label: text
texts.orig: : At the start of each week, take a few minutes to skim your calendar for the week ahead. Any meetings you should cancel? Any discussions you still need to prepare for? Any emails/docs/actions you need to add to your TODO list? Similarly, skim your calendar for the day each morning, and go through the same exercise. It should take literally one minute.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Anticipate asks
texts.text: Anticipate asks

texts.label: text
texts.orig: : Always be asking yourself — What are the next biggest blockers for my team? What is my manager likely to ask of me in the next week? Start working on those things now.
